source.title: Wide Neural Networks Trained with Weight Decay Provably Exhibit Neural Collapse
source.authors: Arthur Jacot; Peter Súkeník; Zihan Wang; Marco Mondelli

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a gradient-descent training-error result using regularized square loss in a restricted network class, rather than testing the claim’s stated benchmark classification-error recipes.
record.gate_note: Theorem 4.4 reports approximate training interpolation under its assumptions. The numerical experiments report neural-collapse metrics, not training classification error; cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional square-loss interpolation for smooth-activation pyramidal networks and measures neural collapse. These results do not test V1's convolutional benchmark classification claim or V2–V6. Section 5.2 uses assumed edge-of-stability behavior to derive conditioning consequences; it does not establish V5's training dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove low square-loss training residual and approximate balancedness under restrictive architectural and optimization assumptions, yielding within-class collapse. Additional conditioning assumptions, justified for global minimizers or conditionally stable large-learning-rate solutions, support class-mean orthogonality and alignment.
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical guarantee for λ-regularized gradient descent on square loss in smooth-activation pyramidal networks, rather than the claim’s benchmark classification-error training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee depends on pyramidal topology, smooth activation and initialization assumptions, and sufficiently small regularization and step size with a specified minimum number of steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Assumptions 4.1–4.3 and equation (10), regularized gradient descent guarantees ∥Z_L^k − Y∥_F ≤ √2ϵ₁.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smooth-activation pyramidal networks with a sufficiently wide first layer achieve approximate square-loss interpolation under the stated initialization, regularization, step-size, and duration conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 5.3 derives linear-head conditioning bounds from bounded NTK, approximate interpolation, and bounded weights; Section 5.2 connects these to assumed edge-of-stability behavior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For approximately interpolating networks with bounded weights, an NTK bound constrains conditioning of products within the linear head.

record.problems: The result is conditional on restrictive assumptions, including smooth activations, pyramidal topology, a specific initialization condition, and small learning rate and regularization. It does not report benchmark training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant training-error outcomes were reported. Neural-collapse metric plots and cited prior-work results do not report the claim’s training classification-error outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error of large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 under SGD or Adam from random initialization, including corrupted labels and size, stopping, or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU training, spurious local minima frequencies, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-related training error in plain versus residual networks, longer-training controls, and the initialization exceptions.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, divergence boundaries, and sharpness trajectories during full-batch training.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports equation (25), despite the record's failed excerpt match. The record's ICLR 2024 publication attribution is not established by the supplied manuscript.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, convolutional architectures, SGD or Adam, and the stated size, duration, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima frequencies, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual shortcut comparisons and depth-related training classification error.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above a stability threshold, curvature changes during training, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: network satisfying Assumptions 4.1–4.3
rows.size_stated: Pyramidal topology: n₁ ≥ N and n₂ ≥ n₃ ≥ … ≥ nL; width otherwise not stated.
rows.stage_stated: Gradient descent from initialization satisfying Assumption 4.3; random initialization not stated.
rows.operation_detail: λ-regularized gradient descent on square loss, with step size and training duration satisfying Theorem 4.4.

conditions.value: k satisfying the lower bound in (10)

rows.note: The theorem guarantees this residual for the specified network class and parameter conditions. This is a square-loss interpolation result, not a reported training classification-error result on a benchmark.
rows.check: The residual bound is correctly recorded in Appendix B, equation (25), but it does not measure any stated version. The subject should explicitly include fully connected networks ending in at least two linear layers. The theorem establishes its own interpolation result; 'observed' cannot describe evidence for a linked claim version here.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
